page.overview:
Who is Donquixote Rosinante?

Donquixote Rosinante was a former World Noble of the Donquixote Family descent, being the second son of Donquixote Homing and the younger brother of Donquixote Doflamingo. After his family lost their status as Celestial Dragons and became pariahs, Rosinante was discovered by Sengoku and enlisted into the Marines, eventually reaching the rank of Commander. Upon reuniting with Doflamingo, he feigned muteness and operated as an Elite Officer of the Donquixote Pirates, serving Doflamingo under the codename Corazon while remaining an undercover Marine.

Rosinante abandoned his post in an attempt to cure Trafalgar D. Water Law of his Amber Lead Syndrome. He eventually obtained the Ope Ope no Mi, forcing Law to eat it and thus giving him the means to save himself from the disease. However, his cover was blown by the former Corazon, Vergo, and he was subsequently executed by Doflamingo. Rosinante's kindness and sacrifice would serve as driving motivators for Law to one day avenge him by defeating Doflamingo.

Rosinante was a tall man (standing just below his brother at 293 cm); in adulthood, he was a comparable height to his older brother Doflamingo (who stands 305 cm). He had short, shaggy golden-blonde hair, pale skin (tanner in the manga, much like his brother), and sharp, reddish-brown eyes. He wore a dark red hood from which two heart-like shapes hung, a pair of beige jeans (white in the anime), a very dark-purple feather mantle much like his brother's, and a white shirt with pink hearts printed all over it. He also wore mismatched shoes. His hair was styled longer than his brother's, as it came close to his eyes. Rosinante had dark red lips reaching from his mouth to his cheeks in lines—over his right eye was a dark blue, heavy, eight-pointed rectilinear star tattoo. He also wore sunglasses, though he did away with these upon his 6-month-long journey with Law.

During his childhood, Rosinante had his hair in an unkempt fashion, covering his eyes. Prior to leaving Mary Geoise, he wore the typical garb of the Celestial Dragons and had his hair in the same style as his older compatriots. After leaving, his hairstyle changed, and his wardrobe consisted of simple yet fine clothes with a frilled cravat that became very ragged due to the uneasy lifestyle he had to endure. Suffering from torture at the hands of the locals who hated the Celestial Dragons, as well as other battles, left scars and stitches all over his body. Upon joining the Marines, Rosinante wore the standard cadet uniform, minus the makeup/tattoos he had when working as a spy.
